name: python-frontend-open-points
body: Open design points for the plan/user (do NOT invent decisions here). (1) Module FQN namespace form — DECIDED (language rooting, Human decision folded into the scanner-optimisation change-set): the rendered Python Module FQN is the language-rooted form `py.<dotted-identity>` — the language-namespaced option. Python package identity is the init-bearing dotted name; under the language root `py` it is disjoint from every other language's module namespace (a root package `apg` renders `py.apg`, distinct from Rust's `rust.apg`) and from markdown's rooted absolute paths, so cross-language collision-freedom and collision-freedom for package-qualified dotted identities hold by construction. The root does NOT make flat init-less modules globally unique: a flat module's identity is its stem alone, so `a/foo.py` and `b/foo.py` both render `py.foo` and the second is silently shadowed — flat modules are unique only within their directory (requirements.requirement.python-package-identity). See requirements.requirement.language-rooting and domain.value.module-fqn-prefix; the earlier alternatives (bare dotted FQN, a path-derived absolute-path form like markdown's) are superseded by the root. (2) Cython / .pyx — pinned OUT of the accepted set (python-accept-extensions) because `ty` cannot parse Cython exactly; whether a future Cython frontend or a tree-sitter heuristic arm is wanted is a user call. (3) uv/venv project-context model — `ty` resolves imports against a project environment; how the frontend models that environment (a uv project, a venv, a bare src root) governs whether third-party imports resolve to external UnresolvedTargets or are treated as in-project. The scan/emit half is settled, not assumed: `site-packages` (like a virtualenv) is an explicit discovery exclusion — NOT a scan root, emitting no code nodes (domain.constraint.python-exclusions) — yet remains available to `ty` as a resolution input in the full project context (global.constraint.frontend-full-context). The open part is only how the frontend supplies that excluded tree as `ty`'s environment input. Deferred. (4) Ruff/ty pin currency — the reference pins ruff tag 0.16.6; whether that tag's ty API still matches current main's needs, and the policy for bumping the pin atomically (as src/rustlib does for rust-analyzer), is a plan-time build decision. (5) Incremental target-set acceptance — the exact target-set/delta interface a frontend receives (per-file vs per-package) and the granularity of the ty/salsa cache under targeted emission are the incremental-content plan's concern (requirements.note.open-design-points); Python's per-module granularity interacts with the package identity model and is not decided here.
